top3.headline: Thinking Machines ships Inkling 2 Small on Tinker
top3.whyItMatters: A 594B MoE with 17B active scores 31 on AA and targets long-horizon agent work.

top3.headline: Julius DeepFinance grades models on real PE deals
top3.whyItMatters: Top models clear only about half of multi-day diligence rubrics leaders actually use.

top3.headline: Airbnb plans an AI trip agent for first-half 2027
top3.whyItMatters: A major travel platform is betting on composed travel UI, not a chatbot, for booking.

items.title: MIT reviewer books Tau's teleoperated cleaning robots
items.takeaway: Tau's SF humanoids are remote-piloted via head and wrist cameras; pricing moved from about $30/hour to $60/week for two.
items.soWhat: Home humanoids are selling teleop data collection today, not autonomy you can trust yet.

items.title: Cursor's poteto: skip the software-factory pitch
items.takeaway: poteto says factories are marketing; spend tokens where work is deterministic. Huntley still drives loops by hand at about $43k/week of inference.
items.soWhat: Agent ROI may come from disciplined token spend and determinism, not a new factory product category.

items.title: Meng To builds a BG3-style game in three.js with Opus
items.takeaway: A month on and off with Claude Opus 5.5 and three.js; about $10k in tokens; Tripo3D for character rigs; local Mac app over a 100MB+ browser build.
items.soWhat: Serious AI game craft is becoming a token budget and tooling problem, not a demo weekend.

items.title: Naval: attention, not money or time, is life's currency
items.takeaway: Naval amplified his line that what you choose to notice and act on is the scarce resource that compounds.
items.soWhat: Investor framing of scarcity still starts with attention allocation before capital or calendars.

items.title: Perplexity staff get 7x more Teammates agent-hours
items.takeaway: Aravind Srinivas says median weekly agent-hours from Teammates are 7x September; one in five staff already hit 40+ hours.
items.soWhat: Internal agent load is compounding weekly; headcount plans need an agent-hours line, not only seats.

items.title: Airbnb plans an AI-native trip agent for 1H 2027
items.takeaway: Q3 letter: agent composes maps, photos, comparisons, calendars, and itineraries in real time, then books inside Airbnb with co-travelers.
items.soWhat: Consumer agents that ship will look like product UI assemblers, not chat boxes bolted onto search.

items.title: Thinking Machines launches Inkling 2 Small multimodal MoE
items.takeaway: 594B total / 17B active; AA Index 31; live on Tinker now; Apache 2.0 weights planned next week after safety testing.
items.soWhat: Another lab is shipping a long-horizon agent model you can fine-tune today, with open weights promised soon.

items.title: Julius DeepFinance tests models on real PE and IB deals
items.takeaway: 21 multi-day diligence tasks; Opus 5.5 max leads at 54.8% mean rubric; GPT-6 Astra close behind; Inkling 2 Small at 29.8%.
items.soWhat: Finance automation still stalls near half marks on the workflows that decide real deals.

items.title: Multimodal-SEA benchmarks agents against social-engineering fraud
items.takeaway: 608 expert tasks from real fraud cases across 14 domains score agents on tool-execution outcomes, not free-text judgments.
items.soWhat: Personal agents that can act need multimodal red-team scores before you trust them with money or access.

items.title: NVIDIA paper: short contexts via compaction keep accuracy
items.takeaway: Belcak et al. find frontier models lose little on long-horizon tasks when contexts stay short; later tokens can cost up to about 7x earlier ones.
items.soWhat: Agent stacks may win more from frequent compaction than from ever-longer context windows.
